newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela, Japan agreement on Venalum not finished.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela, Japan agreement on Venalum not finished.

text.p: The Venezuelan government has still not concluded talks with a Japanese consortium that owns 20 percent of aluminum smelter Venalum over its veto power in the company, the Venezuelan Investment Fund (FIV) said Thursday.

The two sides reached a "memorandum of understanding" after three days of talks in New York, but a signed agreement which specifies compensation for removing the veto power has yet to be concluded, the FIV said in a release.
The memorandum of understanding will be signed within the next few days once translations of the document have been drawn up, the release added.
The FIV welcomed the agreement in principal reached Thursday as a breakthrough which would "open the doors to successfully culminate the privatization of the aluminum sector."
Earlier Thursday Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff had said that the Venezuelan and Japanese owners of Venalum had reached an agreement.

The government wants the Japanese consortium to drop its veto power in Venalum -- the most attractive of its four-company aluminum sector -- before it offers a controlling stake in its aluminum sector to investors in December.

The Japanese consortium which owns the 20 percent stake in Venalum includes Showa Denko KK, Kobe Steel Ltd, Sumitomo Chemical Co Ltd, Mitsubishi Materials Corp, Mitsubishi Aluminum Co Ltd and Marubeni Corp.

The FIV announced last week that 13 companies had qualified to bid for the four-company aluminum sector including Aluminum Company of America (Alcoa), Gencor Ltd, Glencore Ltd, Reynolds Metals Co, Norsk Hydro ASA, and RTZ Corp-Cra Ltd.
